items.stem: A buyer evaluates a bid on price, quality, delivery, quantity and place. Which procurement concept is being applied?

options.rationale: Correct: the five rights (right quality, quantity, place, time, price) frame how procurement delivers value.
Kraljic positions items by risk and spend, not these five criteria.
TCO sums lifetime costs; it is not this five-part framework.
The cycle is a sequence of stages, not these evaluation criteria.

items.explanation: Correct: the five rights (right quality, quantity, place, time, price) frame how procurement delivers value.
items.domain_ref: Added value from procurement and supply

items.stem: At which stage of the sourcing cycle is a detailed specification normally finalised?

options.rationale: Specifications must be set before tenders are sought, not after award.
Correct: a clear specification is prepared before suppliers are invited to bid.
Contract management monitors performance against an agreed specification.
Payment is a post-delivery activity unrelated to specifying need.

items.explanation: Correct: a clear specification is prepared before suppliers are invited to bid.

items.stem: Which TWO activities are part of the post-contract-award phase of the procurement cycle?

options.rationale: Correct: performance management is a post-award, contract-management activity.
Drafting the ITT happens before award.

options.text: Conducting supplier appraisal of shortlisted bidders
options.rationale: Appraisal of bidders happens pre-award during selection.

options.text: Reviewing and closing the contract at end of term
options.rationale: Correct: contract review and closure is a post-award activity.
